titulo: The gate: run, ask, or refuse
lead: A read command doesn’t need the same decision as a command that writes a file. The gate classifies before running; the audit shows what ran and what was refused. The chosen policy changes when the assistant asks: perigosos (dangerous), sempre (always) or nunca (never).
objetivo: Identify the three command classes and check one refused request and one approval request in the audit.
hero_alt: Editorial photography showing the safeguard at work: it runs, asks, or refuses.

nos.detalhe: Commands on the read-only list, such as ls, cat, and pwd, run with the default perigosos policy.
Any command outside the read-only list, or one that writes a file, asks for approval. In the demo, the owner doesn’t approve.
Known destructive patterns, such as rm -rf / and variants, never run.

secoes.legenda: Classification is not a complete guarantee against every unknown command; the sandbox limits what it can reach when you need to run something new.

secoes.sub: Click each step to see what to do.

texto: Only what’s on the read-only list runs directly. Everything else asks for approval; this is safer than a short list of forbidden words.

With the default policy, perigosos (dangerous), read-only commands like ls or cat run unasked; anything that writes asks “rodar …? [s/N]”. Type n or press Enter to refuse; s approves. With the sempre (always) policy, it asks before ANY command, even ls and cat. With nunca (never), read-only commands run, but anything that would need approval is refused without asking. A command blocked by the safeguard never runs under any policy.
A pipe is when you send ready-made text to the program instead of typing in the terminal. In that case, the approval request is refused because no one can answer the interactive prompt.

The audit prints one JSON line (a record with named fields) per event. In the command line, comando is the request; classe is allowed, approval required, or blocked; rodou is true if it ran; decisao explains why. Tool-type lines record the tool used.

secoes.titulo: Commands to observe, with no risk
secoes.sub: Use the mock brain to make sure the tool is called. In the interactive terminal, answer n or press Enter. With llama3.2, asking for a command may not call the tool.

blocos.rot: Terminal · conversation with mock brain and approval
blocos.conteudo:
cd ~/intelecto-v2
python3 -m intelecto conversar --provedor mock --aprovacao perigosos

blocos.rot: In the conversation · ask it to write a file

abas.html:
[aprovação] rodar 'echo teste > nota.txt'? (substituição de comando ou redirecionamento para arquivo) [s/N]

n or Enter refuses; s approves. The audit records "classe": "aprovar", "rodou": false and "decisao": "o dono não aprovou".

The program prints this in Portuguese, exactly as shown.

recusado: precisa de aprovação (substituição de comando ou redirecionamento para arquivo) e a política é 'nunca'

The program prints this in Portuguese, exactly as shown.

secoes.sub: Follow the steps in order and check each one only after you’ve confirmed the result.

exercicios.titulo: Refuse a file write in the terminal
exercicios.texto: Open the conversation with --provedor mock --aprovacao perigosos. Ask “run: echo teste > nota.txt”. When [s/N] appears, answer n (or press Enter). Run auditoria -n 20 and find that request.
exercicios.pronto: The request’s JSON line contains "classe": "aprovar", "rodou": false, and "decisao": "o dono não aprovou"; that request did not create nota.txt.

exercicios.texto: Run python3 -m intelecto demo and identify the classes in the final block. The demo uses a temporary folder and is not included in the audit of your installation.
exercicios.pronto: You mark free as ran, approve as didn’t run, and blocked as didn’t run.

secoes.sub: Choose before opening the explanation. If you get it wrong, use the link to review.

perguntas.p: Which demo command runs without asking?
perguntas.explica: ls is on the read list. Writing requires approval; deleting the root is blocked.

perguntas.p: What does the “nunca” (never) policy do with an action that needs approval?
opcoes: Asks once and runs by default
Refuses anything that would need approval
perguntas.explica: “Never” means nobody approves anything beyond read-only actions: write actions are refused, even with the owner present.

opcoes: Class, command, and whether it ran
The password used by the vault
perguntas.explica: The command line records the class, decision, and execution. The vault does not publish the password.

itens.texto: Dangerous is the default: known reads pass; writes ask. Always asks about every command. Never refuses anything that would need approval.
The audit shows both the refusal and the execution.
